title: The rise of ‘cozy coloring’: Finding calm in simplicity
titleZh: 当世界太喧嚣，一支彩笔也能让人安静下来
summary:
当阿曼达·鲁尔顿随手买了一本便宜的填色书和几支彩笔时，她从没想到自己会将这件事一直坚持下去。那时，她正经历一场健康危机。18个月前，她因感染被紧急送往医院——先后接受了两次手术——此后又多次住院。鲁尔顿，来自英国利物浦，现年28岁，她说道：“那段时间我的心理状态几乎彻底崩溃了。我完全没办法再做那些曾让我觉得快乐的事情。所以，能抽出时间安静地坐下来，专注做点轻松、不会带来痛苦的事，对我帮助很大。这就像是给自己一个喘息的机会，从纷扰的一切中抽离五分钟。”

来源：CNN网站；作者：Carolyn Conway；原文发布时间：2025-10-11 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: When Amanda Rulton picked up a cheap coloring book and some felt-tip pens, she didn’t expect the activity to stick. It came when she was in the middle of a health crisis. Eighteen months ago, she had an infection and was rushed into emergency surgery — twice — followed by numerous hospital stays. “My mental health has completely collapsed,” said Rulton, 28, from Liverpool, in the UK. “I can’t do the hobbies I once enjoyed, so having time to sit and be present in something that isn’t strenuous or causing me harm has been really helpful. It’s about taking five minutes away from everything.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 当阿曼达·鲁尔顿随手买了一本便宜的填色书和几支彩笔时，她从没想到自己会将这件事一直坚持下去。那时，她正经历一场健康危机。18个月前，她因感染被紧急送往医院——先后接受了两次手术——此后又多次住院。鲁尔顿，来自英国利物浦，现年28岁，她说道：“那段时间我的心理状态几乎彻底崩溃了。我完全没办法再做那些曾让我觉得快乐的事情。所以，能抽出时间安静地坐下来，专注做点轻松、不会带来痛苦的事，对我帮助很大。这就像是给自己一个喘息的机会，从纷扰的一切中抽离五分钟。”

paragraphs.contentEn: For Rulton, coloring turned into a daily routine. She began posting videos of her sessions to her TikTok account @gremlinsafari, and stumbled onto ColorTok, TikTok’s growing community of adult colorers. On her account, she shares “color with me” videos — quiet, cozy clips of her filling in pages — alongside updates on her recovery, coping strategies, and the coloring tools she’s testing. Much of what fills her feed belongs to what TikTok users call “cozy coloring” — pages with thick outlines and soft themes, designed for slow, low-pressure evenings. It’s the same bold, easy style dominating ColorTok right now.
paragraphs.contentZh: 对鲁尔顿来说，填色已逐渐融入了她的日常生活。她开始在自己的TikTok账号（@gremlinsafari）上分享自己的填色视频，并因此偶然加入了一个正在壮大的成年填色爱好者社群——ColorTok。她会在账号上发布“和我一起填色”的视频——画面安静温馨，记录她一点点填色的过程——同时也更新自己的康复近况、心理调适方法，以及正在尝试的填色工具。她主页上的内容大多属于TikTok用户口中的“治愈系填色”（cozy coloring）——这类图案线条轮廓粗重、主题柔和，专为那些希望在夜晚放松身心、享受慢节奏的人设计。而这种醒目又简单的填色风格，正是当下ColorTok社群的主流。

paragraphs.contentEn: Coloring books for adults aren’t a new phenomenon. As historian Katherine Ott notes in The Public Domain Review, early “paint books” were marketed to grown-ups in the late 18th century, often framed as educational or moral tools. Satirical adult coloring books surfaced in the 1960s, but adult coloring really caught on around 2015, when Johanna Basford’s intricate drawings in her books “Secret Garden” and “Enchanted Forest” became sensations. That year, sales of adult coloring books in the US jumped from around 1 million to more than 12 million copies, according to Nielsen BookScan data from the 2015 US Book Industry Year Review.
paragraphs.contentZh: 面向成年人的填色书并不是新鲜事物。正如历史学家凯瑟琳·奥特在《公共领域评论》中指出，早在18世纪末，初版的“绘画填色书”就已经面向成年人销售，常被定位为教育或道德启蒙工具。到了20世纪60年代，成人涂色书开始出现带有调侃风格的版本，但真正掀起填色热潮的，是2015年前后乔汉娜·贝斯福推出的畅销作品《秘密花园》与《魔法森林》。据尼尔森图书调查在《2015年美国图书产业年度回顾》中发布的数据，当年美国成人填色书的销量从约100万册猛增至超过1200万册。

paragraphs.contentEn: They seem to be going strong. TechSci Research reported the global adult coloring market to be worth $151 million in 2024, with it projected to reach $320 million by 2030. But recently, a “cozy coloring” aesthetic has dominated adult coloring charts — simple line art with large shapes meant for quick, relaxing fills. Coco Wyo, a leading publisher that dominates bestseller lists, markets a Bold & Easy line for adults. Of Amazon’s best-sellers in October 2025, nearly half of the top adult coloring books emphasized the “bold & easy” style — a pull toward accessibility over intricacy, intended to soothe tired minds.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这股风潮仍在持续升温。根据TechSci Research的数据，2024年全球成人填色市场规模已达1.51亿美元，预计到2030年将增长至3.2亿美元。不过，近来主导成人填色市场的，是一种被称为“治愈系填色”的美学风格——其特点是线条简单、色块宽大，适合快速填色与轻松解压。长期占据畅销榜的头部出版商Coco Wyo也顺势推出了面向成年人的“Bold&Easy”（加粗简易）系列。在2025年10月的亚马逊畅销榜上，排名前列的成人填色书中近一半都强调这种“Bold&Easy”风格——表明市场趋势正从繁复精致转向轻松易上手，旨在为疲惫的心灵带来片刻慰藉。

paragraphs.contentEn: A London-based independent illustrator who posts on TikTok under the alias Miss Kitsch, who didn’t want us to use her real name in this article, has watched the market shift firsthand. Her books blend bold outlines and soft, whimsical scenes that evoke nostalgia and calm. She said her books are designed to feel “comforting” rather than complex, reflecting a growing demand for simplicity in adult coloring.
paragraphs.contentZh: 一位在TikTok上以“Miss Kitsch”为名发布作品的伦敦独立插画师（她不希望在本文中公开真实姓名）亲眼见证了市场的这一转变。她的填色书融合了粗线条轮廓与温柔梦幻的场景，能够唤起人们的怀旧情感与内在的宁静。她表示，自己的作品并不追求复杂构图，而是希望带来一种“令人安心的”体验，这也恰好反映出当前成人填色市场对简约风格的日益偏好。

paragraphs.contentEn: “When I first started, my focus was on kids and teenagers,” she said. “But I quickly realized coloring books are hugely popular amongst adults. Today, the majority of my audience is adults, so I like to think of my books as a way to nurture the inner child within all of us.” She said the nostalgia is powerful: “Many customers tell me that coloring makes them feel like a little kid again. For adults, it’s not only a way to unwind after a busy day, but also a chance to reconnect with creativity they may not have explored since childhood.”
paragraphs.contentZh: Miss Kitsch表示：“刚开始时，我的创作重心是面向儿童和青少年的。但我很快发现，填色书在成年人中同样非常受欢迎。如今，我的读者大多是成年人，所以我更愿意将这些作品看作唤醒并滋养我们每个人内心童真的一种方式。”她还提到，怀旧情绪的力量十分强大：“很多顾客告诉我，填色让他们重新找回童年的感觉。对成年人来说，这不仅是忙碌一天后放松身心的方式，也是一种重新拾起童年时期那份久违创造力的途径。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Ciara McCabe, professor of neuroscience at the University of Reading, in the UK, said research is catching up with what hobbyists already feel. “We know that people who engage in hobbies and leisure activities have lower rates of depression,” she said. “If you have a good social network, you’re less likely to develop disorders like depression. We know hobbies work.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 英国雷丁大学神经科学教授席亚拉·麦凯布指出，相关的科学研究正逐步印证许多兴趣爱好者早已亲身体会到的益处。她解释说：“我们知道，经常参与兴趣活动或休闲活动的人，抑郁症发病率相对较低。如果一个人拥有良好的社交圈子，那么患上抑郁等心理疾病的风险也会更小。我们已经可以确定，培养兴趣确实有效。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Coloring, she suggested, works because it’s low stakes. “All you have to do is keep in between the lines. That’s actually very relaxing because it’s taking away all the other things we have to worry about on a daily basis.” And it’s not just soothing, but protective. “Hobbies, social connections, doing stuff that’s pleasurable, motivating, something that gives your life purpose — those are protective factors. They can help prevent depression in the first place.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 她指出，填色之所以有用，关键在于它几乎不构成心理压力。“你只需要把颜色涂在线条之间。这个过程本身就很解压，因为它能让人暂时摆脱日常生活中那些需要操心的事情。”填色不仅能带来平静感，也具有一定的心理保护作用。“培养兴趣、维系社交、从事那些让人愉悦、激发动力、赋予生活意义的活动——这些都是保护性因素。能够从源头上降低抑郁的风险。”

paragraphs.contentEn: For Girija Kaimal, professor of the Creative Arts Therapies at Drexel University, in Philadelphia, and author of “The Expressive Instinct: How Imagination and Creative Works Help Us Survive and Thrive,” coloring’s appeal runs deeper than nostalgia. Kaimal’s insights stem from her 2019 small study of 39 adults, which found that just 45 minutes of art-making reduced negative emotions and increased feelings of self-efficacy — even among those with no prior art experience.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在费城德雷塞尔大学创意艺术治疗学教授、《表达的本能：想象力与创作如何助我们生存与成长》一书的作者吉里贾·凯玛尔看来，填色的吸引力远不止于唤起怀旧情绪。凯玛尔的观点源于她在2019年针对39名成年人进行的一项小型研究，结果发现，仅45分钟的艺术创作即可显著减轻负面情绪，并增强参与者的自我效能感——即便是没有艺术训练背景的参与者也能从中受益。

paragraphs.contentEn: “I think of us as 21st century hunter-gatherers. Our bodies and minds are tens of thousands of years old. We worked with our hands; we used all our senses. Coloring takes us back there,” she explained. As for why it feels rewarding, “by the end of it, you have something colorful — and colorful signals health to us,” she explained. “In nature, when you see color, it usually signifies abundance; a fertile landscape.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 她解释说：“我常将现代人比作是21世纪的‘狩猎采集者’。我们的身体与心智早在数万年前就已演化完成。那时，我们依靠双手劳作；调动全部感官。而涂色能让我们回到那种原始状态。”至于为什么这种活动会让人感到愉悦，她补充道：“当你完成一幅填色作品时，眼前是色彩斑斓的画面——而色彩对我们而言，本身就意味着生命力。在自然界中，鲜艳的色彩通常象征着丰饶；一片富足的景象。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Kaimal said the move toward simpler, more structured pages reflects how “we’re all looking for respite from stress.” “Coloring takes away that pressure of a blank slate,” she explained. “It has a structure — you’re set up for success.” She added that this kind of activity “lets people play again,” giving them a safe way to create without fear of failure. And skill doesn’t matter. “Just the act is going to activate reward pathways. If you’re reflective about it, that deepens the effect. But either way, we should allow ourselves some silliness and fun.” Kaimal added. “We are allowed to play as adults, however silly.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 凯玛尔指出，人们越来越倾向于选购更简单、结构更清晰的填色页，这其实反映出“我们都在寻求一种从压力中暂时抽离的方式”。她解释说：“填色消除了面对空白画纸时的心理负担。它自带了框架——让你更容易获得成就感。”她补充道，这类活动能“让成年人重新学会玩”，为人们提供一个安全的创作空间，无需担心失败。至于技巧，她认为并不重要。凯玛尔补充道：“光是动手填色这个行为本身，就能激活大脑的奖赏机制。如果你能在过程中有所思考和体会，效果会更明显。但无论如何，我们都该允许自己去做些轻松、有趣的小事。即便我们是成年人，也同样拥有玩耍的权利——哪怕看起来有点幼稚也没关系。”

expressions.expression: …… surfaced in ……, but …… really caught on around ……, when …… became sensations.
expressions.meaning: ……在……时期出现，但直到……年才真正流行起来，那时……成为了轰动一时的现象。
expressions.example: Podcasts about true crime surfaced in the early 2000s, but the genre really caught on around 2014, when Serial became a sensation.
expressions.exampleZh: 关于真实犯罪的播客在21世纪初就已出现，但这一类型真正走红是在2014年前后，当时《Serial》成为现象级作品。

例句：Podcasts about true crime surfaced in the early 2000s, but the genre really caught on around 2014, when Serial became a sensation.
